We consider the impact of different regularization operators on the inversions, and enforcing constraints like mass conservation to improve inversion results.

entries.title: A Study of Three Intrinsically Luminous Long Period Interacting Eclipsing Binaries in the Galaxy and the Small Magellanic Cloud
entries.abstract: The properties of the eclipsing binaries SMC004701.39-732645.8, SMC005609.41-722809.2 and PW Pup are examined using archival photometric and spectroscopic observations. These systems have orbital periods of hundreds of days, and contain highly evolved components with temperature differences of at least 1000 - 2000K. The SMC systems are among the brightest eclipsing binaries in that galaxy at visible wavelengths, and show excess thermal emission that appears to be typical for luminous K and M giants in that galaxy. A preliminary mass function for SMC004701 suggests a minimum mass for the secondary of 3.8 +/- 0.8 Msolar, whereas the PW Pup mass function indicates a minimum mass for the secondary of 3.2 +/- 0.3 Msolar. Light curve elements are examined for a range of mass ratios using observations at visible and mid-infrared (MIR) wavelengths. The results suggest that SMC004701 may prove to be a double line spectroscopic binary at visible wavelengths. However, with the possible exception of emission from a circumstellar disk, infrared observations will likely be required to detect light from the secondary in the other two systems. All three systems have likely experienced mass transfer, and had components with initial masses that correspond to B spectral types on the main sequence. The light associated with the secondary likely originates from a shell or disk that obscures a hotter central star.

entries.title: Self-arresting vortex rearrangements in pinned spinning-down superfluids
entries.abstract: Superfluids, in a spinning-down container with pinning centres, exhibit sudden collective migration of quantized vortices. The onset, progress, and termination of this process remain poorly understood. Here, we show that: 1) the first exodus of vortices occurs when a sector of the vortex array, having a minimum opening angle, is vacated close to the wall; 2) driven by this exodus, the superfluid flow near the boundary continually decreases in strength and arrests the exit; and 3) the resultant depletion region has well-defined dimensions---governed primarily by the critical unpinning velocity, the container size, and the initial rotation rate---that limit the angular momentum transferred to the container. We conclude by discussing the relevance to pulsar glitches.

entries.title: VENUS: A Census of Strong Lensing in a 60-Cluster JWST Survey
entries.abstract: We present strong-lensing models for the 57 galaxy clusters observed in Cycle 4 out of the 60 targeted by the JWST Vast Exploration for Nascent, Unexplored Sources (VENUS) program. Models for the remaining three clusters will be incorporated after their observations. The dataset comprises 5013 individual images, corresponding to 1733 multiply-imaged systems, of which 912 have spectroscopic redshift measurements and 227 are newly identified. Using this new wealth of observations, we construct parametric lens models with our $\mathtt{AstroLensPy}$ software, reproducing the observed image positions with an average image-plane precision $Δ_{\rm RMS}$ of $0.54''$. With a total imaging area of $576$ arcmin$^2$, VENUS offers the largest homogeneous set of cluster strong-lensing models to date. The clusters yield a combined area of $191$ arcmin$^{2}$ magnified by $|μ|\geq3$ for a source $z_s=10$, for example, establishing the VENUS fields as a premier survey for high-redshift studies. Among our sample, the clusters MACS J0717.5+3745, RXC J0600.1-2007 and PLCK G287.0+32.9 display the largest Einstein radii ($\geq 60''$) and magnified areas ($\mathcal{A}_{z_s=10}^{|μ|\geq3} \geq 9$ arcmin$^2$) for a source $z_s=10$, and therefore constitute the most potent gravitational telescopes known to date. Finally, leveraging the statistical power of the sample, we derive scaling relations between various lensing observables (Einstein radius, magnified area, projected mass) and the SZ/X-ray-inferred cluster mass, $M_{500,c}$.

analysis.reason: Investigates the collective rearrangement and self-arresting unpinning of quantized vortices in pinned spinning-down superfluids, providing theoretical mechanisms and scaling relations for pulsar glitches.
analysis.result: Vortex exodus is triggered when the sector opening angle reaches a critical threshold $\phi^{*} = \frac{3\pi v_{\text{crit}}}{2R\Omega_{0}}$, and self-arrests as depleted-sector counter-circulation reduces the wall flow below $v_{\text{crit}}$, producing a container spin-up $\Delta\Omega_{c}^{*} = \Omega_{0} \left[ \frac{I_{s}}{I_{c}} \frac{{d^{*}}^{2}}{R^{2}} \frac{\phi^{*}}{\pi/2} \left(1 - \frac{d^{*}}{2R}\right)^{2} \right]$ with $\Delta\Omega_{c}^{*}/\Omega_{0} \sim 10^{-10}$ estimated for the Crab pulsar.
analysis.reading_entry: Self-arresting vortex rearrangements in pinned spinning-down superfluids
analysis.problem: How quantized vortex avalanches in pinned, spinning-down superfluids trigger, spatially propagate, and self-arrest, and what physical scaling laws set the resulting glitch spin-up amplitude.
analysis.method: Analytical modeling using image vortices and angular momentum conservation combined with 2D Barnes-Hut tree point-vortex simulations on a cylinder of radius $R$, initial angular velocity $\Omega_{0}$, and vortex density $n_{v}\kappa = 2\Omega_{0}$ with critical unpinning speed $v_{\text{crit}}$.
assumptions: Vortices remain straight line-like filaments neglecting three-dimensional turbulent tangles
limits: Two-dimensional point-vortex formalism neglecting 3D vortex curvature, Kelvin waves, and realistic neutron star crust-core coupling elasticity
citation_leads: Self-arresting vortex rearrangements in pinned spinning-down superfluids: “reflecting as a spin-up in the container’s rate of rotation.”
Self-arresting vortex rearrangements in pinned spinning-down superfluids: “getting recaptured only upon entering a sub-critical region.”
A.1 Velocity field at the tip for small sector depths: “The first unpinning leads to a small sector, of depth $d$ and opening angle $\phi$, devoid of vortices”
B.1 Superfluid simulator: “This two-dimensional formalism hinges on treating vortices as point-like entities”
analysis.research_progress: Demonstrates an intrinsic self-arresting mechanism where counter-circulation from the vortex-depleted sector suppresses the boundary tangential velocity below $v_{\text{crit}}$, terminating the avalanche and establishing the scaling $\Delta\Omega_{c}^{*} \propto \Omega_{0} (I_{s}/I_{c})(d^{*}/R)^{2} \phi^{*}$.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Schematic of the superfluid flow in the presence of a sector devoid of vortices. Striped region indicates a vortex-free zone, with the rest of the container having a uniform distribution of vortices. Blue dashed arrow conveys the container’s direction of rotation. Blue and orange solid arrows specify the initial tangential flow and the effect of the sector, respectively. Purple arrowheads indicate the direction of flow on the contours of the vacated region due to the missing vortices. Left) Perturbation - A small sector near the boundary, of depth $d$ and opening angle $\phi$, is depleted of vortices, increasing the tangential flow at the tip. Right) Recapture - The sector is much larger than it was initially, now described by a depth $d^{*}$ and an opening angle $\phi^{*}$. The net flow at the tip is above critical, whereas that at the wall (where the forward arm of the sector meets the boundary) is exactly zero.
figures.label: Fig. 1
figures.physical_core: Schematic of the superfluid velocity field perturbation and recapture geometry caused by a vortex-free depletion sector of depth $d$ and opening angle $\phi$. As the vacated region expands to $(d^*, \phi^*)$, the induced counter-flow reduces the net tangential velocity at the boundary to zero, providing the physical mechanism that arrests the vortex exodus.

figures.caption: Figure 2: State of the vortex array, as observed in simulations, at the end of the exodus (left) and at the end of the entire event (right), arranged from top to bottom, increasing in $v_{\text{crit}}$ (30, 60, 90). Black dots represent vortices. Pinning sites, more numerous than the vortices, are not shown. In all the cases, the radius of the container R=10. The opening angle $\phi^{*}$ and the depth $d^{*}$ recorded at the end of exodus increases with $v_{\text{crit}}$. However, the total depth of the disturbance, apparent at the end of the entire event, is seen to reduce with $v_{\text{crit}}$.
figures.label: Fig. 2
figures.physical_core: Numerical simulation snapshots of the quantized vortex array during spinning-down, comparing the state at the end of the exodus against the end of the complete event across critical unpinning velocities $v_{\text{crit}} \in \{30, 60, 90\}$. It demonstrates that the depletion sector dimensions $(d^*, \phi^*)$ grow with $v_{\text{crit}}$, while the total disturbance depth contracts.
